$$ |f(X) - f(X')| = \left| \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{x_i}{i} - \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{x'_i}{i} \right| $$
Since $x_j = x'_j$ for all $j \neq k$, the terms cancel out except for the $k$-th term:
$$ |f(X) - f(X')| = \left| \frac{x_k}{k} - \frac{x'_k}{k} \right| = \frac{1}{k} |x_k - x'_k| $$

Therefore, the maximum change occurs when the first element changes from 0 to 1 (or vice versa):

$$ \varepsilon_{actual} = \frac{\Delta f}{b_{given}} = \frac{1}{1/(2\varepsilon)} = 2\varepsilon $$
